newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak insurer SP says privatisation must proceed.
newsitem.headline: Slovak insurer SP says privatisation must proceed.

text.p: The privatisation of Slovakia's largest insurer, Slovenska Poistovna a.s. (SP) should proceed as soon as possible, the TASR news agency quoted SP President Edita Bukovska as saying on Wednesday.
"The complete privatisation (of SP) should take place as soon as possible within...one and a half years, but urgently by the end of 1998," Bukovska told TASR.
SP officials were not immediately available for comment on Bukovska's statements nor its privatisation.
In early March parliament approved a law cancelling the selloff of state stakes in Slovenska Sporitelna, the largest savings bank, and SP until December 31, 2003.
Through the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, the state controls 50.5 percent of SP.
But Bukovska said SP is already suffering from the lack of a "real owner" able to put funds into the firm over the next four or five years.
"From a pragmatic point of view, domestic subjects, including perhaps two or three new shareholders, will be probably involved and preferred in the next (SP) privatisation moves," Bukovska said.
Foreign investors would be offered participation in privatisation only if there were no domestic interest, she added.
"They (foreign inestors) should take part mainly by increasing the basic capital of SP to allow it to make profits from those funds," Bukovska said.
She said funds from the sale of the state stake would be used to restructure SP's loan portfolio, as it had provided "considerable volumes" of bad loans between 1992 and 1993.

Last June Poistovna was the centre of a crisis inside Slovakia's ruling coalition after a boardroom fight resulted in two separate managements, each evicting the other and occupying company headquarters.
